news.title: World Cup co-hosts US and Canada oppose FIFA’s Gianni Infantino
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino waving on arrival for the swearing-in of Colombia's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, in Cali, Colombia, on Aug 7. LOS ANGELES – The football federations of the United States and Canada – two of the 2026 World Cup host nations – on Aug 10 backed a statement from three confederations criticising FIFA president Gianni Infantino. US Soccer, Canada Soccer, the CFU (Caribbean Football Union) and UNCAF (Central American Football Union) said they “stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens FIFA’s governance, transparency and accountability”. That puts the US and Canada at odds with the third co-host of this year’s World Cup, Mexico, which has given Infantino its backing.

news.title: CommBank Young Socceroos Squad for the AFC U20 Asian Cup China 2027™ Qualification phase confirmed
news.lede: Australia will face Laos, Malaysia and Indonesia as they look to secure their place at the AFC U20 Asian Cup China 2027™, where the continent’s representatives for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027™ will be determined. The qualification phase also provides players with valuable competitive international experience, an opportunity to build momentum ahead of the domestic season, and a platform to showcase their talent to a broader international audience. The 23-player squad features a strong domestic presence, with 17 players drawn from Australian clubs, while a further six are based with clubs in Europe and Japan.

news.title: Performers to have hydration breaks during parade
news.lede: People performing in the Battle of Flowers this Friday will be given hydration breaks every 25 minutes to help deal with the hot weather. Organisers said walking and working around the floats could be physically demanding and with the heat set to reach 27C (80.6F), according to Jersey Met, it will be necessary to have breaks. The Battle of Flowers Association announced its fireworks finale would go ahead on Saturday despite a higher risk of wildfires, whilst private displays have been cancelled due to the dry summer Jersey has experienced. The association said, like the football World Cup, water breaks would last three minutes.

news.title: Trump backs Infantino after fury over FIFA chief’s World Cup sale plan
news.lede: It would be a “terrible mistake” to replace the football boss after the success of the 2026 World Cup, the U.S. president posted on Truth Social. President Donald Trump backed under-pressure football chief Gianni Infantino, after calls grew for the FIFA boss to quit following his aborted plan to sell off parts of the World Cup tournament to private investors. “FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino. He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented,” Trump posted Tuesday morning on Truth Social.

news.title: FIFA Accused Of 'Deception' In Fresh Attack Over World Cup Rights: 'Fundamental Breach Of Trust'
news.lede: Football’s three major continental confederations have accused FIFA president Gianni Infantino of committing a “fundamental breach of trust” after his failed effort to sell an interest in the World Cup to private equity investors. UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC made the accusation in an “open letter to the football family” released on Monday, escalating the backlash against Infantino and his leadership of the sport’s global governing body. The three organisations also said that “when trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.” UEFA oversees football in Europe, CONCACAF represents North, Central America and the Caribbean, while the AFC governs the sport in Asia.

news.title: US President Donald Trump issues backing for under pressure Fifa chief Gianni Infantino
news.lede: US President Donald Trump was awarded the Fifa Peace Prize by Infantino in 2025. US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position. Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

news.title: ‘Terrible mistake’: Trump backs Infantino after explosive letter revealed
news.lede: Updated August 11, 2026 - 4.53am. First published August 10, 2026 - 10.05pm. Long-time supporter of Gianni Infantino, US President Donald Trump has explosively backed the FIFA president, posting on his Truth Social account that the federation would “be making a terrible mistake” if they replaced him. The post came after the European football’s governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF issued an open letter attacking the FIFA chief’s conduct during the proposed sale of a stake in World Cup commercial rights.
